description: September 2025 Periodontal Pearl: Assessing and Diagnosing Periodontal Disease • What is periodontal health? • What is periodontal disease? • How to assess periodontal disease? • Stage and Grade Periodontal Health What is periodontal health? Periodontal health is the state of the supporting parts of periodontium to include the gingiva, periodontal ligaments, cementum, and alveolar bone. These parts are assessed by the measurements of clinical attachment level [CAL], probing depths, bone loss, mobility, recession, and bleeding on probing to evaluate the presence of signs and symptoms of periodontal disease. A healthy periodontium is usually uniformed pink in color variations based on race, fits snug around the teeth, stippled in texture, sharp papilla that fills interdental space, and absence of disease and inflammation. What is periodontal disease? Periodontal disease is a chronic inflammatory disease of the periodontium that is caused by infectious bacteria. The two most common inflammatory oral infections are gingivitis and periodontitis. Gingivitis is produced by induced biofilm and plaque and non-induced biofilm and plaque [genetics; viral; fungal; immune conditions; reactive processes; neoplasms; endocrine nutritional, and metabolic diseases; traumatic lesions; and gingival pigmentation] infections that are confined to the gingiva. ¹ The gingiva is generally characterized as painless, redness, swollen, bleeding and tenderness to touch with the absence of periodontal attachment loss, bone loss, and mobility, and can be reversed to a healthy state. Backflow can occur when: • There is pressure in a patient’s mouth [a result of closing their lips and forming a seal around the tip of the ejector] that is less than in the saliva ejector [similar to how liquid flows back into a cup after drinking through a straw]. • The suction tubing attached to the ejector is positioned above the patient’s mouth. • A saliva ejector is used at the same time as other evacuation [high-volume] equipment. Recommended Practice 1. Instruct patients not to close their lips around the saliva ejector. Instead, they should allow it to rest passively in the mouth or corner of the lips. 2. Use single-use disposable ejectors and discard after each patient. 3. Flush evacuation lines with cleaning solution or water between patients. 4. Use anti-retraction valves or backflow-prevention devices on dental units.

description: Updates 2025 - Answers to Prosthodontics Specialty Panel Questions 1. Compare and contrast the literature supporting traditional pressed fixed restorations vs milled and 3D printed fixed restorations. • First to address 3D-printed fixed restorations [crown & bridge]: 3D-printed fixed restorations are currently used primarily for provisional fixed restorations, although there are new methods becoming available to 3D-print ceramic restorations as well. With regard to provisional crown and bridge restorations, there is a systematic review and meta-analysis available from 2022 [Jain et. al., 2022, Polymers ] that reviewed and analyzed research done comparing 3D-printed provisionals to milled and conventional provisionals, and they concluded that, in general, while 3D-printed provisionals do have a few drawbacks, [i.e. color stability and water sorption], they have superior fracture strength and wear resistance. They concluded 3D-printed provisionals are a good clinical alternative to milled or traditional materials for provisionals. With regard to 3D-printed zirconia crowns vs milled zirconia crowns, there are relatively new materials and technology to 3D-print zirconia crowns; there is systematic review and meta-analysis from 2024 [Alghauli et. al., 2024, Journal of Dentistry] that concluded that both 3D-printed and milled zirconia crowns had acceptable internal and marginal fit, both had the usual zirconia strength, but with 3D-printed crowns having superior esthetics; other studies showed 3D-printed zirconia crowns have a microscopically rougher surface than milled crowns, but otherwise both manufacturing techniques led to clinically acceptable crowns. title: March Specialty Pearl: Endodontics-Resorption
description:
March 2026 Dental Pearl: Endodontics-Resorption Root resorption is the pathological loss of dentin or cementum from the tooth root, initiated by clastic cells [osteoclasts/odontoclasts] due to trauma, infection or pressure. [NIH.gov] There are 2 broad categories of resorption internal and external. The categories are based on where the resorption originated from. In children, the roots of deciduous teeth naturally undergo resorption as part of the normal physiological process. Root resorption in permanent teeth is almost always a pathological process. 2 things need to happen for root resorption to occur: 1] there must be a loss of the protective unmineralized surface layers of the tooth adjacent to dentin 2] there must be active on-going inflammation next to the exposed dentin. Internal Root Resorption -Usually asymptomatic, lesion is usually symmetrical oval size enlargement of the pulp space, and part of the pulp tissue must be vital for this process to be active, chronically inflamed pulp tissue, when the canal becomes necrotic the resorption stops. -Treatment includes conventional root canal therapy often with intracanal medicament to eliminate the resorptive tissues, prognosis is very predictable and favorable. Coined“pink tooth of Mummery” by James Howard Mummery. Types of External Root Resorption: External Inflammatory Root Resorption -Presence of sulcular bacteria, pressure from adjacent impacted teeth and pressure from orthodontic tooth movement were found to be associated with inflammatory root resorption. Once etiology was removed this would lead to the arrest of the active resorptive process. -Preventative and interceptive strategies can be employed to treat/stop the inflammatory root resorption. Learning objectives: 1] Know what root resorption is. 2] Learn what two conditions are required for root resorption. 3] Know what predisposing factors could cause ECIR

title: IC Tip of the Week: Don’t Top Off Those Disinfectant Wipes
description:
This is based upon the tip of the week e-mail sent out by DOH the week of July 14th, 2026. To gain CDE credit, participants must successfully pass a test [score 80] based upon the reading material. Reading Materials: https://www.cdc.gov/dental-infection-control/hcp/summary/sterilization-disinfection.html https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/disinfection-sterilization/summary-recommendations.html https://www.cdc.gov/dental-infection-control/hcp/dental-ipc-faqs/cleaning-disinfecting-environmental-surface.html https://www.epa.gov/coronavirus-and-disinfectants/about-list-n-disinfectants-coronavirus-covid-19 The CDC States: Disinfectants must be used exactly as directed, including proper dilution, preparation, and use conditions. Altering a product [such as adding liquid to wipes] is inconsistent with labeled instructions and may reduce effectiveness. DHCP should follow manufacturer recommendations for use of products selected for cleaning and disinfection [e.g., amount, dilution, contact time, safe use, and disposal]. Improper preparation [including dilution changes] can impact disinfectant performance. Solutions should be prepared exactly as directed and not altered. Disinfectant efficacy depends on correct concentration. Adding liquid [topping off] can dilute the active ingredient and compromise microbial kill. Disinfectants should be prepared fresh and according to manufacturer recommendations; improper handling or storage can reduce effectiveness. The EPA States: EPA-registered disinfectants are only effective when used according to their label. The label is legally enforceable—modifying the product [like adding fluid] is considered misuse.
Learning objectives: Upon reviewing the NIPCS Tip of the week, you will: 1. Understand the importance of not diluting disinfectant solution 2. Know what role EPA plays in our use of disinfectants 3. Understand key considerations when dealing with bloodborne pathogens
accreditation: Indian Health Service Division of Oral Health

title: IC Tip of the Week: Honoring Contact Time [Wet Time]?
description:
This is based upon the tip of the week e-mail sent out by DOH the week of July 28th, 2026. To gain CDE credit, participants must successfully pass a test [score 80] based upon the reading material. Reading Materials: https://www.cdc.gov/dental-infection-control/hcp/summary/sterilization-disinfection.html https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/disinfection-sterilization/summary-recommendations.html https://www.cdc.gov/dental-infection-control/hcp/dental-ipc-faqs/cleaning-disinfecting-environmental-surface.html https://www.cdc.gov/healthcare-associated-infections/hcp/cleaning-global/procedures.html?utm_source https://www.epa.gov/pesticide-registration/selected-epa-registered-disinfectants https://www.epa.gov/coronavirus-and-disinfectants/about-list-n-disinfectants-coronavirus-covid-19 The CDC States: Disinfectants must remain on a surface for the full contact time specified on the label to achieve the intended antimicrobial effect. If a surface dries before the required contact time, the disinfectant may not achieve proper microbial kill. Shortened exposure times may result in incomplete disinfection and survival of microorganisms. If the surface dries before the required contact time, additional disinfectant should be applied to maintain wetness. The EPA States: EPA-registered disinfectants must be used according to label directions, including specified contact times. Different disinfectants have different required contact times depending on formulation and target organisms. The FDA States: All disinfectants must be used exactly as directed, including application method and duration of exposure.
Learning objectives: Upon reviewing the NIPCS Tip of the week, you will: 1. Understand the importance of not diluting disinfectant solution 2. Know what role EPA plays in our use of disinfectants 3. Understand key considerations when dealing with bloodborne pathogens
accreditation: Indian Health Service Division of Oral Health

title: IC Tip of the Week: Don’t Forget to Clean Before You Disinfect
description:

title: August Specialty Pearl: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Orthodontics
description: August 2026 Dental Pearl: Orthodontics Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Orthodontics The American Association of Orthodontists recently updated their 2019 white paper on obstructive sleep apnea. This is a summary of that paper, with the original attached. While the paper is addressed to orthodontists, the information provided is essential to all dental providers. There is growing recognition of orthodontists' role in screening for obstructive sleep apnea [OSA] and contributing to its multidisciplinary management in both children and adults. Sleep-related breathing disorder [SRBD] is the term used to encapsulate multiple conditions ranging from snoring to obstructive sleep apnea. This document focuses primarily on OSA. Obstructive sleep apnea occurs when the upper airway repeatedly collapses during sleep due to increased airway collapsibility and reduced neuromuscular tone, causing breathing interruptions, drops in oxygen levels, and frequent sleep arousals. In children, they have additional exacerbating factors like lymphoid hyperplasia and growth-related changes that can impact the upper airway. These events trigger increased heart rate, blood pressure, and cardiovascular stress, often recurring many times throughout the night. OSA has a multifactorial etiology involving craniofacial anatomy, neuromuscular function, obesity, hormonal changes, fluid shifts, and genetic factors, resulting in wide variation in disease severity and treatment needs among patients. Although obesity increasingly contributes to childhood OSA, affected children may also be underweight due to growth restriction or failure to thrive; therefore, OSA risk assessment is recommended in children regardless of weight. OSA affects an estimated 14 of men and 5 of women, though it is likely underdiagnosed and

description: Fighting Resistance: The Dental Professional’s Role in Antibiotic Stewardship The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is a growing concern, with new strains emerging that are increasingly difficult to treat. As antibiotic use increases, their effectiveness diminishes. In this engaging presentation, attendees will gain insights into the current state of antibiotics, learn about appropriate usage, and explore non-antibiotic alternatives for patient treatment. Review and apply current prescribing guidelines. Discuss penicillin allergy testing and its impact on reducing antimicrobial resistance. Assess and implement non-antibiotic products and protocols for patient care.

title: Infection Control
description: Breaking the Chain: Mastering Infection Control Basics Ensuring infection control compliance can be challenging for many practices. Staying compliant with infection control protocols is one of the most critical—and complex—responsibilities in dental practice today. From keeping up with evolving OSHA regulations and CDC guidelines to ensuring thorough team training, waterline maintenance, and proper sterilization, the demands are high and ever-changing. Add in cost management and effective documentation, and it’s easy to see how practices can feel overwhelmed. But noncompliance isn't just risky—it can be devastating. The consequences include potential patient or team infections, legal and financial repercussions, and lasting damage to your practice’s reputation. This course provides practical strategies and updates to help dental teams navigate infection control with confidence, protect those in their care, and maintain the trust of the communities they serve. Learning objectives: 1. Define infection prevention principles and recommendations for dental health care settings 2. Recognize how to prevent transmission of infectious agents through standard precautions, with a review of cross-contamination prevention, hand hygiene, respiratory hygiene, and cough etiquette. 3. Employ standard operating procedures to remain in compliance with regulation, which includes PPE and practitioner safety, sharps safety, safe injection practices, and environmental controls. 4. Formulate a successful dental unit waterline protocol, including dental unit water quality and waterline testing. 5. Manage a successful infection control plan that includes sterilization of patient care items to prevent disease transmission.

title: The Infection Control Reset: Back to Basics with CDC Guidelines
description: Amanda Hill RDH, received approval to deliver This CE Activity by the Maryland Department of Health, Dental Board, on December 3, 2025. MSDBE CE Course Number: 2025-0087. As CDC guidance evolves and regulatory expectations continue to increase, dental teams must stay prepared to protect patients, coworkers, and themselves from the spread of infectious diseases in the clinical setting. title: AIRWAY MANAGEMENT: Treating the Hot Air + Tongue Ties in Airway Therapy
description: Course Overview Current data notes 90% of adults are breathing incorrectly, contributing to over 60% of adults constantly falling short of the appropriate amount of sleep. Additionally, it is estimated that upwards of 90% of individuals with sleep apnea are currently undiagnosed. For perhaps the first time in history, society is actively inquiring about how to maintain personal health and wellness prior to falling ill. These unique pivots are now creating a call to action across dentistry, elevating patient expectations and curating new conversations within the dental practice. While discussing preventive dentistry or attempting to treat asymptomatic disease previously brought patients to question the ‘hot air’ in treatment planning, it is widely recognized that society has become a captive audience in understanding preventive modalities. As the daughter of a woman lost to undiagnosed airway complications, Katrina M Sanders curates an approach aimed to assist dental providers in identifying appropriate airway profiles while addressing the all-too-common ‘tongue tie’ oftentimes experienced when attempting to communicate with patients about airway obstructive disorders. Don’t leave critical airway conversations up in the air; breathe easier with clear patient identifiers and medical history evaluation strategies aimed to create a lasting therapeutic care plan aimed to manage airway and subsequent sleep complications. title: Periodontal Pathogens Beware! – Unique Chemo-mechanical Strategies to Create and Sustain Oral Homeostasis and Support Systemic Health
description: Overview Patient-centered care is not new. It is our “why”. Current research supports coupling conventional therapy with innovative products that enhance clinical care and set the stage for improved health outcomes. Pathogenic biofilms play a huge role in the development, and exacerbation, of inflammatory periodontal disease. Dysbiotic biofilm communities are difficult to disrupt and eradicate. For years clinicians have searched for ways to make professional debridement easier and more effective. Novel therapies such as desiccation shock technology provide a new option to effectively treat and eradicate pathogenic biofilm communities. Desiccation therapy, using a sulfonated compound, is an effective tool that can be used in a wide range of clinical challenges. The desiccation process disrupts biofilm EPS, affects how deposits attach to a surface microscopically, and destroys polymicrobial communities. Effective desiccation therapy results in a coagulum full of denatured calculus, necrotic tissue, and blood. Learning Objectives Identify how periodontal pathogens create and support a dysbiotic biofilm community and understand the role of microbial persisters in chronic oral infections. Examine the role of desiccation shock therapy in biofilm dysregulation, debris removal, and hemostasis and learn how to recreate a thriving, sustainable, healthy oral microbiome. Learn how desiccation therapy improves clinical outcomes, speeds up healing, improves patient comfort, reduces clinician MSD stresses, and adds a valuable clinical service to the treatment plan.

title: The Road to Edentulism, and Back
description: This course reframes edentulism as a functional disability with measurable systemic health implications, rather than simply a dental misfortune. Participants will examine the documented links between tooth loss, removable prostheses, and systemic comorbidities while critically comparing traditional denture paradigms to fixed full-arch implant solutions in terms of function, biomechanics, quality of life, and long-term satisfaction. The program concludes with evidence-based treatment planning principles and a prosthetically driven, multidisciplinary workflow for immediate full-arch rehabilitation. Describe the documented associations between tooth loss, removable prostheses, and systemic comorbidities. Critically evaluate traditional denture-based treatment paradigms versus fixed full arch implant solutions, comparing functional outcomes, quality of life metrics, biomechanical efficiency, and long-term patient satisfaction. Apply evidence-based principles for full arch implant treatment planning, including implant number, distribution, axial loading, cantilever management, and the role of tilted implants in reducing biomechanical stress. Outline a prosthetically driven, multidisciplinary workflow for immediate function full arch rehabilitation.

title: SS by Anne O. Rice, RDH - Addressing the Sleep Deprivation Crisis in Dentistry
description: Course Overview Sleep serves as a fundamental pillar for the proper functioning of all bodily systems. It plays a dynamic role in bolstering the immune system, allowing immune cells and proteins to effectively combat infections. Sleep helps balance insulin and glucose, vital for metabolism, and regulates appetite by affecting hunger and satiety hormones, assisting weight management. Sleep is directly linked to cardiovascular health, contributing to lower blood pressure and reducing the risk of heart-related issues. Adequate sleep is essential for mental well-being, staving off anxiety and depression and promoting a better mood. There is no significant organ or bodily process that does not benefit from optimal sleep. With more than 20,000 scientific studies highlighting the advantages of a complete night\'s rest, yet 30% of adults are sleep deprived, it is evident that tackling sleep deprivation is one of the foremost health challenges of our era. The dental community is uniquely positioned to contribute to helping the sleep loss epidemic by screening for sleep-disordered breathing, educating patients, or treatment. By embracing this expanded role, dental professionals can significantly impact the health and quality of life of their patients. Learning Objectives * Examine the role of sleep, including its stages and processes, as a as a fundamental aspect of all body systems. * Discover what could be the worst science experiment we are doing to our children. * Gain insight into essential sleep functions related to memory consolidation and the elimination of brain toxins. * Acquire a comprehensive understanding of nasal breathing, mouth breathing, and the function of nitric oxide.

title: Periodontal Therapy with Purpose
description: Course Overview Periodontal Therapy with Purpose reframes instrumentation as more than just calculus removal. When we instrument, we do it methodically and with intention—addressing not only deposits but the broader disease process. This comprehensive course explores biofilm removal and management, reduction of inflammatory mediators, preservation of cementum, smear layer removal, and strategies for minimizing bacteremia risk. Participants will learn about the innovative use of desiccation technology—a therapeutic approach that enhances antimicrobial effectiveness, reduces inflammation, and supports root surface health. The course also emphasizes supporting the commensal oral microbiome through adjunctive probiotics, promoting a balanced ecosystem that enhances long-term periodontal stability. Together, these approaches create a purposeful, evidence-based pathway to optimal patient outcomes. Learning Objectives At the conclusion of this 2-hour course, participants will be able to: Differentiate between the goals of calculus removal and comprehensive biofilm management in periodontal therapy. Incorporate desiccation technology into periodontal therapy protocols for antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory benefits. Explain how reducing inflammatory mediators supports healing, decreases tissue destruction, and contributes to long-term periodontal stability. Describe the importance of preserving cementum and tooth structure to maintain attachment, support regeneration, and prevent sensitivity. Evaluate the impact of smear layer removal on root detoxification, reattachment potential, and overall treatment outcomes. Assess the potential of probiotics in supporting commensal bacteria and restoring microbial balance in periodontal care.

title: Orofacial Pain: Relief for the General Dentist and the Hygienist
description: Course Overview In March of 2020, the American Dental Association approved the Application for Specialty for Orofacial Pain, making Orofacial Pain the twelfth recognized specialty of the ADA. Orofacial Pain covers seven general areas that are not addressed in detail by any other recognized dental specialty. The seven tenets of orofacial pain include temporomandibular disorders, neuropathic pain like trigeminal neuralgia, neurovascular pain like migraines and temporal arteritis, muscular pain and dysfunction, primary headaches, atypical dental pain, psychological aspects of pain, and sleep. This course is designed to raise awareness of the many patients that may be suffering from undiagnosed orofacial pain in the typical dental and medical practices. Learning Objectives Upon the completion of this course, attendees should be able to: • Identify the seven general topics of Orofacial Pain • Be able to recognize which cases in their own practice may be appropriate for consideration of referral to an orofacial pain specialist. • Understand that pain patients are unique in complexity, even when the diagnosis may seem simple. • Be familiar with evidence-based concepts for the management of temporomandibular disorders.

title: SPOTS: Five ways to spot a myofunctional disorder
description: Course Overview As highly trained dental professionals we screen and assess for many oral disorders and health problems for optimal patient care. The participant will get a look into myofunctional therapy, which is an individualized program designed to tone and coordinate the orofacial complex. Normalizing good oral development and function includes restoring the correct functional and rest patterns of musculature affecting occlusion, breathing, swallowing, speech, and TMD. SPOTS is the acronym and screening tool developed by the speaker to aid the clinician in easily identifying myofunctional disorders in the clinical setting. We will look at how Speech, Posture, Occlusion, Tethered oral tissues, and Swallow affect our patients. Learning Objectives Upon completion, the participant will be able to understand and identify how speech, posture, occlusion, tethered oral tissues and swallow can affect oral and facial development Upon completion, the participant will be able to use the SPOTS screening tool for their clinical practice and patient education Upon completion, the participant will be able to identify how TMJ disorders can be affected by myofunctional influences Upon completion, the participant will understand how the position of the tongue, and its functions, affect the orofacial structures, airway, and body posture

description: Course Overview Explore the cutting-edge scientific research revealing the profound effects of nutritious foods and their components on the oral microbiome. With nutrition misinformation rampant, it can be difficult to separate fact from fiction. This course will debunk the myths relating to nutrition and oral health and describe the current available evidence on how nutrition can support oral homeostasis. Oral health practitioners will leave this presentation with a comprehensive understanding of the role of a healthy dietary pattern, as well as the ability to incorporate these considerations into conversations to provide a patient-centered approach to oral healthcare. Learning objectives • Discuss intricacies of the oral microbiome • Gain insight into the bidirectional relationship between nutrition and the oral microbiome • Discuss the evidence-based research regarding how diet influences both oral and systemic health • Delineate ways to incorporate nutrient-dense foods into the diet to optimize the health of the oral microbiome

title: Agents of Change: How Dental Hygienists Can Drive Eco-Friendly Prevention and Early Intervention

From minimizing waste in the operatory to selecting eco- friendly preventive products and utilizing cutting-edge technology, this course will empower dental hygienists to reduce their environmental impact while improving patient care. Attendees will delve into the benefits of early intervention, caries risk assessments, and digital wellness scans, all framed within a sustainable approach. The course emphasizes the importance of aligning oral care with planetary health and fostering a preventive mindset among patients. By taking a leadership role in promoting environmentally friendly practices, dental hygienists can make meaningful contributions to the reduction of healthcare- related pollution, enhancing both oral and overall health outcomes. Link preventive oral care to the broader concept of planetary health. Educate patients on the environmental benefits of early prevention.

Health care professionals, including dentists, dental hygienists and dental assistant, should understand the evolving pattern of illicit drug use in the U.S., as well as the types of drugs being diverted and abuse, to provide safe dental treatment to patients who may be affected by Substance Use Disorder (SUD). This program updates dental professionals on the current status of the Opioid Epidemic, the recognition of SUDs in dental patients, the implications of SUDs for patient management, and reviews non-addictive drugs that can be used in place of opioids for dental pain management. 2 hours C.D.E. Course Objectives: Review the scope and current status of the opioid epidemic and related issues; Understand methods that the dental team can use to identify patients with Substance Use Disorder (SUD); Review the dental management of patients with specific types of SUD; Recognize and prevent potential adverse drug-drug interactions when treating patients with SUD; Review appropriate drug therapies for managing pain and dental infections in patients with SUD; Utilize effective tools for patient communication about opioids and other controlled substances.

title: The Mental Dental Connection: The Secret to Being a Better Clinician and Leader
description: Course Overview Dental professionals often examine the physical aspects of wellness yet we rarely explore or discuss the mental aspects. It is time to remove the taboo and face the facts. Anxiety, pain, depression, burnout. Dentistry can be difficult and take a toll. Studies show us that dental professionals experience a high incidence of mental illness. Additionally, many dental professionals don't clearly understand the mental health conditions that our patients present with, which red flags to watch for or what to do/how to intervene. Presented in Dr. Joshua Austin's trademark comedic style, this course explores strategies for working together to improve mental health so we can be our best. Learn how to recognize triggers and warning signs. Identify essential tools and resources. Discover how and when to refer to a mental health professional. Explore and understand mental health terms, common treatments and therapy options. Gain coping mechanisms and learn how to manage expectations - both our own and those of our patients. Learning Objectives • Define mental health terms and analyze mental health statistics • Discover mechanisms for coping with our personal and professional challenges • Illuminate common DSM-5 diagnoses and characteristics • Learn how to choose the professionals for our own personal wellness team • Identify and examine our psychologic triggers and their importance • Explore the benefits of psychotherapy • Consider today to be Dental Mental Health Day!

title: Obesity, Ozempic and Oral Health
description: Course Overview Obesity is a pressing health issue in the United States, affecting approximately 42% of adults and significantly increasing their risk for type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, stroke, and various cancers. This condition also poses a heightened risk for periodontal disease, a concern for dental professionals. With around 6% of the population currently using weight loss medications like Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy to manage their blood glucose levels, and the recent FDA approval of tirzepatide (Mounjaro and Zepbound) for chronic weight management, it is essential for dental practitioners to stay informed about these developments. This course will equip dental professionals with the knowledge and skills needed to effectively address the unique challenges posed by obesity and weight loss medications in their practice, enhancing patient care and outcomes. Learning Objectives Upon completion of this course, the participants will be able to Define obesity and its correlation with increased risks of periodontal disease and other oral health issues. Discuss the various weight loss medications available, including their mechanisms, benefits, and potential side effects Assess the implications of obesity and weight loss medications on dental care, including the need for medical consultations, potential modifications to routine dental care, and considerations for sedation and oral hygiene instructions. Evaluate strategies for providing nutritional counseling and motivational interviewing (MI) to support patients in managing their weight and improving their overall health.

title: Minimally Invasive Dentistry: Modern Strategies for Caries Management
description: Course Overview Minimally invasive dentistry is transforming caries management by shifting the focus from surgical intervention to prevention, remineralization, and preservation of natural tooth structure. This course reviews the science of demineralization and equips clinicians with the latest tools to detect early lesions before cavitation occurs. Participants will explore evidence-based strategies, including the use of silver fluorides, self-assembling P11-4 peptides, hydroxyapatite-based agents, povidone-iodine, and calcium/phosphate technologies. Through case-based discussions and practical applications, clinicians will learn how to integrate these advances into daily practice, empowering patients with at-home tools to support remineralization and long-term oral health. Learning Objectives At the conclusion of this course, participants will be able to: Explain the demineralization and remineralization processes and their role in caries progression and prevention. Identify early signs of demineralization using modern diagnostic tools and risk assessment strategies. Evaluate the clinical application and mechanisms of silver fluorides, P11-4 peptides, hydroxyapatite, povidone-iodine, and calcium/phosphate products in caries management. Incorporate minimally invasive techniques into treatment planning to halt or reverse dental decay. Discuss evidence-based protocols for supporting patient-centered caries prevention through both in-office and at-home remineralization strategies. Apply case-based learning to integrate minimally invasive approaches into everyday practice.

title: Gaining Horizontal and Vertical Bone with Mineralized Bone Particulate, rh-BMP2 and Resorbable Ultrasonic-Applied Rigid Barriers
description: While many benefits of rh-BMP2 have been described, there is still a need for further evidence and refinement of the overall application. Further, the use of titanium mesh has been well described, but so has the complications of removal and exposure. Bioresorbable barriers are now available which can be molded into any desired three-dimensional form, creating a rigid and resorbable construct that is secured to to the bone using ultrasonic energy. This unique solution has been successfully used to create the proper environment for both large lateral and vertical ridge augmentations for situations previously only treated with block grafting or distraction. Dr. Cummings will share his experience with the material, as well as the key soft tissue techniques that are critical for the success of any large augmentation.

description: Dental Implants have become one of the most predictable therapies in dentistry today. Dental Implants are planned guided by a Prosthetic and Surgical analysis and they always require a Maintenance Therapy by which they can be kept in ideal biology, function and esthetics. The purpose of this seminar is to review the basic and most important aspects to consider in order to achieve a complete Implant Maintenance Therapy. title: Is IV Sedation Right for You and Your Practice?
description: Would IV Sedation be a valuable addition to your practice? This powerful introductory course by a leading expert on parenteral sedation will address the basics of administration and the potential combination with oral sedation, discuss its pros and cons, as well as provide you with an understanding of why IV sedation is a worthwhile consideration on behalf of your patients.

title: Osteo-Immunology & Oxidative Stress
description: This course is designed to provide healthcare professionals, particularly those in regenerative dentistry and implantology, with an in-depth understanding of the integration between Choukroun's techniques, specifically Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF), and the emerging field of osteoimmunology. Participants will explore the principles, methodologies, and clinical applications of Choukroun's techniques while considering the intricate interplay between the immune system and bone biology. \

title: Management of Medical Emergencies in a Dental Environment
Mini FMR Course
description: The ‘Mini FMR’ course offers 21 comprehensive lessons on full mouth reconstructions. You’ll learn to execute a complete protocol for diagnosis, planning, and treating patients with worn teeth. Discover how to treat patients without TMD successfully, and identify those requiring interdisciplinary care. The course includes designing smiles, raising vertical dimension of occlusion, bite registration, preparation through mock-ups, and protecting new reconstructions, all demonstrated through clinical cases from start to finish. \

title: The Semilunar Technique: Bone Harvesting 2.0 for Real Bone Builders
description: At the beginning of every implantological intervention - especially in compromised situations - there is the reconstruction of the intraoral bony defects. For predictable and long-term stable results, the choice of the procedure and the implementation of the technique by the surgeon are of crucial importance. In the presented procedures, the Biological Bone Augmentation (BBA concept) and the Split bone block technique SBBT (according to Prof. Fouad Khoury) are presented, in which preferably the patient's own and vital bone is used as the so-called \\"Gold standard\\". The advantage lies in the osteoinductive and osteogenetic potency of the autologous bone. At the same time, innovative modifications as the Semilunar technique (SLT) are presented, which may represent a facilitation and simplification of the previous methods. In this context, the careful, safe and, at the same, time time-saving harvesting of the bone as well as the safe reconstruction of the defects are discussed in particular.

title: Peri-Implantitis Revisited: The Fundamental Misunderstanding of Cause and Failed Retreatment
description: The development of peri-implantitis after a well executed surgical procedure is always distressing. If it occurs post-reconstruction, it may compromise the final prosthesis and change the prognosis for the case. A decision to treat the disease process rather than removing the affected implant and revising the case can be a difficult decision. The success rates for treatment of more advanced peri-implant infections still remains relatively low. Without understanding the “Mode of Failure”, and the inability to treat the implant surface definitively, may lead to additional failures and ultimate implant loss. This lecture questions the current understanding why implants become infected, and offers potential solutions to retreatment problems.

title: Full Arch All on X
description: Full Arch All on X concepts have continued to dominate the dental implant realm. Concepts such as hard/soft tissue preservation have been abandoned for gross bone reduction and prosthetic tissue replacement. This workshop will discuss the tools and techniques necessary to preserve and enhance hard/soft tissue for predictable FP1-FP3 restorations. Technologies such as pre and post op facial, intra oral and desktop scanning will be reviewed to reduce chair time for prostheticly driven implant planning and simplified 2-3 visit finalization.

title: A Decision Tree for Horizontal Bone Augmentation
description: Bone augmentation is often required to place an adequate number of dental implants in ideal positions for prosthetic support. In addition, adequate bone volume is needed to maintain long term peri-implant health. There are various techniques that are available for bone augmentation including guided bone regeneration, block bone grafting, mesh grafting and ridge expansion. Graft materials include autogenous bone, allografts and xenografts. In addition there are adjunctive materials such as platelet concentrates, growth factors, membranes, tacks and screws. This presentation will guide clinicians using an evidence based decision tree for bone augmentation in preparation for implant rehabilitation. It will also discuss the option of using narrow diameter implants as an alternative to bone augmentation.

title: 3D Ridge Augmentation: A Recipe for Success
description: This course teaches strategies for managing complex dental cases, focusing on the \\"Circle of Choices\\" to guide decision-making. It covers staging difficult cases for predictability, the role of Periodontal Phenotype in treatment planning, and the philosophy that \\"Hopeless doesn’t mean Useless,\\" emphasizing resource optimization for better long-term results.

title: The Evolution of Pet 5 Steps to Success
description: \ Partial extraction therapy has evolved extensively over the years. The initial techniques made the procedure challenging and limited the execution to a limited number of clinicians. Through the development of the technique from analogue to digital and from free hand to guided surgery this has dramatically changed the workflow dramatically. This lecture will cover the fine details and discuss ways to make the techniques predictable and reproducible. \ \ \ \

title: Surgical Implications on Ridge Contours and Soft Tissue Esthetics
description: This presentation describes the importance of following specific parameters of 3D implant placement, tissue reconstruction (both bone and soft tissues), and proper prosthetic managment to achieve clinical success including predictability and longevity. When those parameters are neglected, esthetic and biological complications may occur. A decision tree based on the implant position, presence of not of perimplantitis, and the evaluation of the prosthetic platform, is presented to determine if the case will be solved by keeping the implant or its removal. Several clinical cases are presented to justify the decision tree.

title: Lateral and Vertical Ridge Augmentation By F.I.R.S.T.
Osseodensification and the Crestal Sinus Lift Approach
Different Surgical Strategies in the Aesthetic Zone
description: This lecture is about different approaches in the aesthetic zone, which depend on the dimensions of the ridge, the socket classification, the quantity of soft tissue available, the consequences of an implant failure in hard/soft tissues, and the provisionalization in immediate implant placement.

title: Full Arch Therapy: Clinical Failures and How To Avoid Them
description: The decision on prosthetic design and approach for full arch dental implant therapy can be a challenge to determine. Often patients present with extensive decay or severe periodontal disease such that teeth no longer can be maintained. This presentation aims to outline a decision tree algorithm on planning for these kinds of cases properly to ensure not only implant osseointegration Is successful but ensure long term aesthetic success of the case. Discussion will include how to choose a hybrid approach versus an FP1 approach and when to utilize tooth preservation concepts such as PET to ensure long term esthetic and functional success.

title: Restoring Dental Implant Vitality: A Comprehensive and Systematic Protocol for Revision Therapy in Overcoming Complications
Advancements in Treating Peri-Implantitis: The Role of Laser Technology
description: \\"Advancements in Treating Peri-Implantitis: The Role of Laser Technology\\" is a focused lecture course designed for dental professionals aiming to deepen their expertise in managing peri-implantitis. The course highlights the LAPIP (Laser-Assisted Peri-Implantitis Procedure) protocol, showcasing its effectiveness in treating peri-implantitis through minimally invasive techniques. Attendees will explore the science behind laser technology, learn about its application in decontaminating implant surfaces, and understand how laser therapy can promote tissue regeneration. The lecture will also cover case studies and best practices for integrating Laser Therapy into clinical workflows and its impact on practice growth. By the end of the course, participants will be prepared to implement this advanced laser protocol in their own practices, offering patients cutting-edge care for peri-implantitis.

title: From Protocols to Practice: Unlocking Zirconia's Potential in Full Arch Implant Rehabilitation
description: This course examines the utilization of zirconia in full-arch rehabilitation, presenting a comprehensive overview of the material's properties, clinical applications, and long-term outcomes. The course will delve into the speaker's team's clinical protocol, emphasizing a prosthetic-driven approach and the integration of digital technologies. Participants will critically analyze the current evidence base for zirconia, exploring its advantages and limitations compared to alternative restorative materials. Furthermore, the course will address key factors influencing the success and longevity of full-arch zirconia restorations, including occlusion, framework design, and material selection. Through case presentations and interactive discussions, participants will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to formulate individualized treatment plans for edentulous patients, incorporating the latest advancements in digital dentistry and prosthetic rehabilitation.

title: Esthetic Zone Restoration: Material Selection & Bonding Implications
description: This course provides dental professionals with essential knowledge for achieving optimal aesthetic outcomes while preserving tooth structure. Topics covered include the primary goals of adhesive dentistry, material selection for veneers, and critical steps in the ceramic bonding process. The course also addresses the challenges of bonding to dentin, effective isolation techniques, and methods for removing excess resin cement. Additionally, it explores preferred cements for zirconia crowns and the impact of root canal treatments on bonded restorations. This course equips participants with the knowledge to make informed decisions for successful esthetic restorations.

title: Implant Restorations and Full Mouth Reconstruction
description: This program will highlight the digital workflow of implants and teeth. In addition, they will be components of Abutments, and discussing emergence profile when patients lose teeth, the ones intuition begins to happen, and to restore this in the proper OVD position is paramount. Critical thinking, and all these steps will help the clinician better perform and be more efficient in restoration of teeth and implants.

title: Addressing Clinical Complications and Mistakes
description: This course develops clinicians' ability to differentiate between surgical mistakes and complications in implant dentistry and implement strategies to minimize both in complex cases. It explores biomechanical principles affecting implant stability and guides the selection of evidence-based surgical techniques for managing the atrophic posterior mandible. Learners will also formulate comprehensive treatment plans for failing full-arch restorations using advanced procedures while anticipating and managing potential complications.

title: Shielding Your Practice: Cybersecurity Awareness for Dental Professionals
description: Protecting Patient Data and Ensuring Business Continuity in the Digital Age \ In today's interconnected world, dental practices face increasing cybersecurity threats that can compromise sensitive patient information, disrupt operations, and damage reputations. This essential webinar is designed to equip dentists and their administrative staff with the knowledge and skills necessary to identify, prevent, and respond to cyberattacks effectively. We'll delve into the specific risks facing dental practices, providing practical strategies and actionable steps to fortify your digital defenses. Through real-world examples and clear explanations, you'll gain a comprehensive understanding of how to create a security-conscious environment within your office. \ \ T approach to cybersecurity within your practice.

title: Efficient Class II Correction
description: The SAGITTAL FIRST philosophy is a groundbreaking approach that standardizes, simplifies and shortens the correction of Class II malocclusions at the beginning of treatment, when patients are most compliant. SAGITTAL FIRST is a non-surgical approach to bite correction, with the goal of correcting the bite prior to aligner or fixed orthodontic treatment. Using the SAGITTAL FIRST philosophy, you are able to shorten treatment times - resulting in greater patient satisfaction, improved practice efficiency and ensure long-term stable clinical results.

title: Do I Have Gaps, Cracks and Other Defects in My Teeth or Restorations?
IPG Redefining All on X Implant Capture (Intra Oral Photogrammetry)
description: Dental photogrammetry has transformed digital implant workflows by providing precise, non-contact scanning methods for capturing implant positions with high accuracy. This presentation will explore the evolution of photogrammetry in dentistry, from its early adoption to modern advancements, including Intraoral Photogrammetry (IPG). Attendees will gain insight into how photogrammetry enhances digital implant workflows, improves prosthetic accuracy, and what emerging technologies will shape the future of implantology.

title: Management of Aesthetic and Biological Complications: Should We Keep or Remove the Implants?
description: This course explores the management of esthetic and biological complications associated with implant-supported restorations in the anterior zone. The presentation emphasizes a comprehensive approach based on the \\"triad of success,\\" encompassing precise implant placement, esthetic tissue reconstruction, and meticulous prosthetic management. Participants will learn a systematic decision-making process, considering factors such as peri-implant health, implant positioning, and platform integrity. The modified envelope technique, a minimally invasive soft tissue grafting procedure, will be highlighted as a key tool for optimizing esthetic outcomes. Through case presentations and interactive discussions, participants will develop the skills to diagnose, treat, and prevent complications, ultimately enhancing the long-term success and patient satisfaction with implant therapy in the esthetic zone.

title: Biological & Restorative Management of Complex Cases in the Esthetic Zone
description: Perio-Prostho approach for Immediate Implant Placement with minimally invasive treatment is the desirable way of treatment with dental implants in the anterior zone. Lack or degradation of biological hard and soft tissues can compromise the survival of the implant and the long-term esthetic result. With the correct digital planning for obtain the correct 3d position of the implant with a good selection of the surgical techniques for tissues grafting and the design of the immediate provisional, can overcome this Type 2 defects and obtain more predictable results.

title: Peri-Implantitis: From Prevention to Treatment
description: Peri-implantitis is one of the most challenging complications in implant dentistry, often threatening the long-term success of treatment. This comprehensive course provides clinicians with the knowledge and tools to effectively identify, prevent, and manage peri-implantitis at every stage. \ Participants will learn how to recognize the clinical and radiographic signs of peri-implant disease, assess severity, and determine the most appropriate course of action—whether it's non-surgical intervention, regenerative treatment, or implant removal. The course will also emphasize risk factor management and evidence-based strategies to minimize the occurrence of peri-implantitis before it starts. \ Whether you're looking to sharpen your diagnostic skills or expand your treatment protocols, this course will provide a practical, case-based framework for confidently managing peri-implant complications.

title: Integration of Quantitative Percussion Diagnostics into Daily Practice
Efficiency Meets Biology: Smarter Implant Site Preparation That Boosts Healing—and Your Bottom Line
description: Implant success starts with the osteotomy. Yet conventional site preparation methods often sacrifice time, bone vitality, and healing potential. Prolonged protocols and heat generation disrupt biology—leading to long clinical procedures, delayed integration, and unpredictable outcomes. \ Innovative drilling solutions are changing the equation. By combining biologically driven design with simplified workflows, new-generation drills drive clinical efficiency, reduce thermal risk, maintain native bone, and enable immediate loading with greater confidence. \ Faster procedures. Healthier bone-to-implant contact. Superior patient satisfaction. These advancements not only elevate clinical outcomes, but they also transform efficiency into profitability. Implant site preparation is no longer just routine—it’s a performance multiplier. Implant site preparation has evolved - from a procedural necessity into a strategic advantage.

title: Nix the Scalpel: A New Era of Laser-Driven Precision in Oral and Implant Surgery
description: This presentation explores the revolutionary impact of laser technology in oral, reconstructive, and dental implant surgeries. It focuses on how lasers are replacing traditional surgical tools like scalpels, providing enhanced precision and minimizing the invasiveness of procedures. Attendees will learn about the practical application of lasers in soft tissue management, bone grafting, and dental implant surgeries, which reduces the need for incisions and sutures. The use of lasers results in fewer postoperative complications, less pain, and faster recovery times for patients. Additionally, the presentation covers how laser technology improves the outcomes of reconstructive surgeries and dental implants, making procedures more predictable, efficient, and patient-friendly.

title: B GUIDE CONCEPT FOR PREDICATBLE FP-1 AAPROACH
Treating Esthetic Challenges: Past to Present
Periodontics in the Digital Era: Following My Journey Through Airway Awareness and Digital Workflows
Beyond Osseointegration: Essential Factors for Successful Anterior Implant Placement
description: Successfully placing anterior implants requires a collaborative effort and a deep understanding of critical clinical factors. Ignoring these elements can result in undesirable long-term outcomes. By prioritizing meticulous planning, we can achieve consistently predictable results. Join us in this session as we delve into the vital considerations for effectively planning and placing anterior implants, ensuring your success in this crucial area of dentistry.

title: Options For Severly Atrophic Jaws
description: Implant therapy has gained a mainstream status for our patients. Several patients still are or become severely atrophic for neglect on their part or by failed or failing implant restorations. This leaves the up to date clinician with a dilemma. Here, we will examine the various reasons for the atrophic conditions and look at the solutions. Most of the discussion will be on the maxillary jaw, but nifty solutions exist for severely atrophic mandibles as well.

title: When Bad Things Happen At Work: Implant Disasters and Near-Misses
description: This advanced-level course delves into the complexities of managing implant disasters and near misses, providing a comprehensive overview of the diagnostic, surgical, and restorative strategies necessary to address challenging clinical scenarios. Through a case-based approach, participants will explore the etiology and management of common implant complications, including peri-implantitis, perigraftitis, ridge deficiencies, and aesthetic zone failures. The course emphasizes evidence-based decision-making, incorporating the latest research and clinical guidelines to optimize treatment outcomes. Topics include advanced bone and soft tissue grafting techniques, management of sinus perforations, and strategies for achieving predictable aesthetic results in compromised cases. Participants will gain valuable insights into treatment planning, surgical execution, and restorative considerations for rescuing failing implants and restoring patient satisfaction.

title: Paradigm Shifts In Periodontal and Peri-Implant Plastic Surgery
description: Advancements in scientific and clinical research have transformed how we address soft tissue and bone deficiencies around teeth, dental implants, and future implant sites. This presentation offers a comprehensive review of therapeutic objectives designed to enhance tissue stability, as well as functional and esthetic outcomes. A focal point is the VISTA (Vestibular Incision Subperiosteal Tunnel Access) technique, which entails cutting-edge principles in wound healing and plastic surgery. This presentation will explore evidence-based approaches such as phenotype modification therapy to increase mucosal thickness, as well as strategies for addressing bone and soft tissue deficiencies through staged and simultaneous approaches. Participants will gain actionable insights into how to pursue regenerative goals to improve periodontal and peri-implant health and stability while advancing patient outcomes.

title: The Fully Guided Autogenous Bone Shell Technique
description: Khoury’s Autogenous Shell Technique is a very famous and effective approach to augment alveolar crest deficiencies. One of the main limitation in its application is the skill needed to perform the procedure. The Digital technologies allow to overcome these limits changing completely the technique with tremendous benefits from a clinal point of view. Guided bone harvesting, guided block management and guided shell fixation will be described in detail.

title: Modern Advances in Surgical Dentistry
Periodontics Merges with Craniofacial Orthopedics in Comprehensive Interdisciplinary Care
Success by Design: An Intersectional Treatment Algorithm for Predictable Results
description: Clinicians today have access to an astounding array of new technology, tools and materials to utilize in their increasingly esthetically oriented practices. However, none of them can ensure success if the treatment design is inadequate. This presentation puts an emphasis on identifying the risk factors to successful esthetic outcomes as well as on developing appropriate solutions to overcoming them. A clear blueprint to designing beautiful smiles will be outlined which will incorporate synergistic surgical, restorative and orthodontics techniques aimed at overcoming esthetic challenges and predictably achieving successful results in any environment. In addition, a focus will be placed on the biological, clinical and biomechanical factors that may allow clinicians to simplify implant protocols with minimally invasive surgical protocols and CAD/CAM enhanced restorative dentistry.

title: Demystifying Biological Dentistry
description: The purpose of this course is to explore the core concepts of biological dentistry and how it pertains to implant dentistry.

title: Improving Hard and Soft Tissues Around Implant With New Innovative Techniques
Mesh Bone Grafting for 3D Bone Augmentation
description: This course will discuss the use of mesh bone grafting for vertical and horizontal bone augmentation. Custom titanium mesh has significantly improved outcomes. Custom mesh decreases the surgical time, improves the stability of the mesh and provides a prosthetic guided mesh design for ideal implant positioning. Many studies also suggest a lower rate of mesh exposure can be expected. \

title: Challenges in Peri-Implantitis: Uncovering Modern Tactics
description: This webinar addresses the increasing challenge of peri-implantitis in dental practices. Periodontist and Implantologist Romanos shares insights into the diagnosis, classification, and modern treatment strategies for peri-implantitis. A significant portion of the presentation is dedicated to the GalvoSurge system, a relatively new tool for implant surface decontamination, and Romanos presents a detailed protocol for managing peri-implantitis, incorporating autogenous bone grafts, xenografts, and connective tissue grafts, along with long-term maintenance strategies.

title: Minimally Invasive Restorative Dentistry: Integrating the Digital Workflow
Unlocking the Power of Amnion-Chorion Allografts in Daily Practice
description: Dr. Leavitt explores the versatility of the BioXclude membrane (de-epithelialized, dehydrated amnion-chorion allograft) and its impact on predictable regenerative outcomes in daily periodontal and implant practice. Through a series of real-world clinical scenarios, participants will learn how BioXclude can enhance healing, reduce complications, and simplify treatment workflows. By the end of this session, clinicians will understand how to apply BioXclude membranes across a range of common scenarios to achieve consistent, reproducible results for their patients.

title: Peri-implantitis in the Sterile Implant Package? Where Trust Begins: Clean Surfaces, Clear Standards, Certified Care
description: Participants will gain insight into the scientific methodologies used to evaluate implant quality, including high-resolution SEM/EDS testing, and understand how compromised surfaces may contribute to early implant complications such as peri-implantitis. This comprehensive webinar presents an in-depth look at the CleanImplant Foundation Ecosystem – an initiative at the forefront of implant quality assurance and patient safety. The course will further introduce a growing global patient portal designed to connect patients seeking high-quality implant care with verified dental professionals. Ideal for clinicians looking to elevate their practice standards, differentiate their services, and join a global movement toward safer, evidence-based implantology.

title: Different Surgical Strategies In Esthetic Zone: How To Prevent and Deal with Complications in the Esthetic Zone
description: Placing implants in the Esthetic Zone it’s a very demanding task. To evaluate the hard and soft tissues, the socket classification, the ridge anatomy, ideal 3D implant position and the final prostho is mandatory before beginning surgery. Planning is key and helps us to avoid complications. If complications arise, there is increased risk and the possibility having to perform a second surgery, which is important to consider when managing patient expectations.

title: Essential Digital Tech and AI in Daily Restorative Practice
description: In this webinar, learn the essential technologies and AI that is being used in daily restorative practice. Webinar will include Learn Consultation/Case Acceptance workflows, Smile Makeover workflows, AllonX with PhotoGrammetry, and Grammetry workflows. Webinar will also address teaming with laboratories and specialists in real-time and what Layered Data can do to improve precision and efficiency.

title: Partial Extraction Therapies
description: This lecture will explore the transformative journey of the Partial Extraction Therapy (PET) and, more specifically, the socket shield technique within dental implantology, charting its evolution from freehand methods to the precision of guided surgery. Initially developed to preserve alveolar ridge and soft tissue contours, the socket shield technique has traditionally been considered highly technique-sensitive and variable in its outcomes. Our lecture will focus on how advancements in surgical guidance have enhanced the reproducibility and predictability of this technique.

title: Posterior Maxillary Atrophy in Partial Edentulism: Surgical Treatment Modalities
description: Posterior maxillary atrophy is characterized by the loss of bone and soft tissue, complicating implant rehabilitation. Bone grafting restores volume for implant support, but soft tissue manipulation is essential for graft protection and healing. The modified palatal roll technique enhances connective tissue thickness, while the pedicled buccal pad of fat provides vascularized coverage and volume —crucial in severe atrophy to support bone regeneration and long-term stability.

title: The Prosthetic Advantage: Minimizing Surgical Intervention Through Predictable Design for FP1 Outcomes
description: Course Description \ This lecture explores-prioritizing prosthetic design to minimize surgical intervention while achieving highly esthetic, stable, and long-term predictable FP1 outcomes. Objectives is to see how to reverse-engineer full-arch cases by designing the ideal tooth position, emergence profile, and occlusal scheme first—allowing the surgical approach to become more precise, conservative, and outcome-driven. My goal is to elevate FP1 full-arch results by aligning surgical execution with a prosthetically dominant philosophy—delivering restorations that are not only esthetic but biologically and mechanically sustainable.

title: All on X: Surgical and Prosthetics Aspects in Full Arch Treatment
description: Course Description \ This course provides a comprehensive overview of full arch rehabilitation, focusing on advanced surgical and prosthetic techniques to restore function and aesthetics for patients. Learners are guided through the entire treatment process, from initial data acquisition and diagnosis to material selection and final prosthetic delivery. Emphasis is placed on precise planning, achieving stable implant placement, and delivering predictable, long-lasting results that significantly improve patients' quality of life.

title: The Shield Aesthetic Concept
Contemporary Ceramics, Printable Materials, and the Digital Dental Team: The Optimization of Digital Technologies with the Human Touch
3D Concept for Restorative Material Choice. The Systematic Decision-Making Process for Restorative Material Options
description: The selection of restorative materials remains one of the most critical, and challenging aspects of restorative dentistry. With the ever-expanding range of ceramics, composites, and hybrid materials, clinicians often struggle to apply universal guidelines that fit every clinical situation. The 3D Concept introduces a structured and visual framework that integrates Restorative Materials, Clinical Conditions, and Patient Expectation, providing clinicians with a systematic pathway for restorative material selection. This approach combines current scientific evidence, clinical judgment, and patient-centered considerations into a decision-making tree that simplifies complexity, enhances predictability, and adapts to the unique needs of each patient.

title: Full Arch Precision: A Digital Journey from Surgery to Smile
description: Digital dentistry is rapidly transforming how clinicians diagnose, plan, and deliver implant care. By integrating intraoral scanning, facial scanning with jaw tracking, CBCT imaging, and 3D printing, clinicians can construct a comprehensive digital representation of the patient—the Dental Avatar. This unified ecosystem aligns esthetics, function, and anatomy, forming the foundation for prosthetically driven treatment planning and execution. The presentation examines how this workflow, including intraoral photogrammetry (IPG), enhances data accuracy and supports efficient same-day fabrication of provisional restorations, while also streamlining pathways toward definitive full-arch implant solutions.

title: Elevate Your Practice with Sedation Dentistry
description: In this course, we will look into the powerful ways that IV sedation can help dentists build careers that are both fulfilling and profitable. We will also cover the apprehensions, perceptions, and misperceptions about IV sedation that exist in the minds of dental practitioners. \ More importantly, though, we'll discuss how IV sedation can help create a larger \\"point of entry\\" for patients who need (but might be avoiding) dental care, while significantly improving clinical care and the overall \\"patient experience\\" as well.

title: Hardcore Dentistry: When Digital Precision Meets Biomimetic Serendipity
description: This presentation explores the evolution of digital dentistry and its integration with biomimetic principles to achieve natural-looking and long-lasting dental restorations. We will delve into the journey from early digital technologies to modern advanced techniques, emphasizing patient-centric care and the art of mimicking nature.

title: The Role of TEAM in Reconstructive & Esthetic Dentistry: 30 years in Retrospect
description: Restorative options in anterior tooth replacement. The diagnosis of deficiencies as well as the varied treatment options will be discussed in detail. title: Aesthetic Dentistry and Cosmetic Surgery - A Team Algorithm
description: Where does cosmetic dentistry and cosmetic surgery start and end? This presentation intends to Impart an algorithm when evaluating our patient's facial anatomy and possibilities for both smile and facial aesthetics.

title: Beauty and the Block: Achieving Restorative Control with Chairside Milling
description: By integrating design, milling, and advanced materials, clinicians can deliver efficient, high-quality, single-visit restorations with greater control and predictability. title: Optimally Invasive Implant Treatment Planning: A Restorative-Driven Approach to Surgical and Restorative Success
description: This lecture introduces the core principles of restoration-driven, optimally invasive implant therapy, with a strong emphasis on a patient-centered, biologically sound approach. Attendees will learn how comprehensive treatment planning, combined with advanced diagnostics and digital workflows, supports the right surgical techniques while achieving predictable functional and esthetic outcomes. Emphasis will be placed on starting with the end in mind to guide surgical execution and optimize restorative success.

title: Long-term Esthetic and Functional Success in Implantology
description: This course delves into the critical factors for successful long-term dental implant outcomes, emphasizing the often-overlooked significance of soft tissue integration alongside osseointegration. description: The object of this webinar presentation is to discuss some of the timely employment laws that affect all employers irrespective of size, as no employer is exempt from complying with applicable local, state, or federal employment laws and regulations. The webinar will also include case based discussions to translate concepts into clinical practice, followed by a live Q&A to address participants' questions and real world concerns.

title: Posterior Composites Made Easy
description: Posterior composites are a procedure that shows up on our schedules each and every day. Finding ways to make them more efficient and more effective has been a goal for several decades in dentistry. In this CE webinar we will look at new materials and techniques for accomplishing just that.

title: You Made a Great Impression On Me

title: Beautiful and Predictable Anterior Composites
description: Direct composite can be a conservative, durable and beautiful anterior material. We will discuss the variety of materials and techniques available today to take your composites to the next level so your team and patients are raving about the esthetic results. The CE webinar will compare total etch to self etch techniques and distinguish the risks and benefits of each. The concept of layering for ultimate beauty and color control will be covered and techniques for simplifying direct composite veneers and class four restorations will be presented.

title: Air Polishing vs. Aqueous Powder Streaming
description: Upon completion of this CE webinar, attendees will be able to:• Understand the differences behind stain removal and biofilm management.• Comprehend the differences between first-generation air polishing devices and the newer powder streaming devices. • Identify which air abrasive powders are best for stain removal, biofilm decontamination or both.• Benefits of treating the dental implant population with aqueous powder streaming. • Introduction to adjuncts that improve debridement for both the patient and clinician when practicing aqueous powder streaming. • Implement a new process of dental hygiene care workflow.

title: Predictable and Efficient Class II Restorations
description: This CE webinar will demonstrate, in a step-by-step fashion, how to place sensitivity free composites quickly and easily, with consistently strong contacts, so that an aesthetic result with a high success rate and predictable outcome can be achieved.

title: Mastering Composite Layering and Blending
description: Have you ever felt lost when trying to shade match a difficult tooth color? With dozens of shades to choose from, learn how you can layer one, two or more shades to find the ideal match for every patient in this CE webinar. Blending multiple shades doesn't have to be time-consuming or expensive but can provide an excellent solution for all patients.

title: Enhancing Patient Care and Profits
description: Innovative and reliable professional products offer added value to your patient's oral health. At the same time, the implementation of a product profit center has the potential to add $30K-$60K to the practice's income.

title: The ABC’s of Composite Handling
description: Creating a smooth, functional, and beautiful restoration requires an understanding of function, anatomy and materials. We will explore how using various viscosities of composite can save time and effort, while creating highly esthetic restorations. See how easy it is to replicate the polychromatic shading and realistic characteristics found in natural teeth.”

title: Keep Your Patients Returning
description: Gain a competitive edge by learning how to strengthen your dentist/practice-to-patient relationship with loyalty marketing. Patient retention is dentistry's #1 top management problem. Upon completion of this CE Activity, the student will be able to: provide a workable system that keeps your patients coming back; establish a brand loyalty with your patients to create a strong patient advocate for the brand and your practice in their own social circles and online media

title: Increasing Case Acceptance from Whitening to the Esthetic Dental Procedures
description: As clinical procedures in aesthetic dentistry continue to expand and improve, the dental assistant’s role continues to evolve as well. As we connect with the patient and understand their desires, it allows them to become more open and honest with their expectations. Increasing case acceptance is easy when we know what to ask and say. This CE webinar takes the dental assistant through proper records gathering, treatment planning and case acceptance and how to include whitening and esthetic dental treatment.

title: Bonding For Phased Treatment
description: Have you seen patients that desperately need help, but their life circumstances prevent them from affording ideal dental care? Bonding can be the answer, to get them through life looking nice until their situation improves. Upon completion of this CE webinar, the student will be able to: identify and implement techniques which will allow the dentist to restore anterior teeth with composite

title: The Proper Pre-Bleaching Examination for Optimal Patient Satisfaction
description: Prior to initiating any form of tooth bleaching or whitening, a proper examination should be performed to render a proper diagnosis of the cause of discoloration. This diagnosis guides the treatment times, techniques and materials so that the patient is satisfied with their results, and has realistic expectations for what bleaching can do as well as whether other treatments are needed in addition to or instead of bleaching to achieve the smile they desire.

title: Esthetic Dentistry for Tots and Teens
description: This CE webinar will discuss the use of glass ionomers, resinomers, flowable composites and bulk composites in the restoration of children and teen’s teeth for function and esthetics. In addition various types of crowns will be shown that are available to restore more severe caries on children and adolescents. Esthetic facings for stainless steel crowns will be illustrated and the chairside steps necessary will be given.

title: Lost Opportunities in Hygiene
description: A vital active hygiene department is a key to practice success, maintaining health for our patients, driving the treatment we complete and being a productive component of our business. Maximizing all three of these areas is about creating and maintaining solid systems and minimizing lost opportunities. In this CE webinar we will discuss a variety of ways to reinvigorate your hygiene practice and have it become a key ingredient in practice success.

title: Whiter, Brighter, Healthier Teeth
description: The CE webinar will cover practical techniques for in-office and take home whitening. Fulfilling the desire and demand to have a bright and white smile is the ultimate goal for every dental practice. A bright smile not only presents a healthy and beautiful impression, but also increases one’s interest in oral hygiene, allowing the patient to have more social self-confidence and self esteem. Before the patient can go through the whitening process, we must have a proper whitening consult to understand the patient and their desires.

title: Immediate Loading of Implants and Over Dentures: Treatment Planning, Fabrication, and Delivery
description: In this timely CE webinar we will discuss the various stages in immediate load and over denture appliances. This includes scanning appliances, planning software, immediate pick up of implants, plus the deciding factors in Hybrid bridges and Over dentures.Upon completion of this CE webinar, the student will be able to: understand the basics of CT scanning and scanning appliances; have an understanding of implant planning software and its advantages; identify the pros and cons of Hybrids and Over dentures; be familiar with initial loading and final appliances

title: Complete Denture Technique: The Fundamentals
description: Over the last several years, the complete denture technique continues to receive less emphasis in North American undergraduate dental school curriculums. Consequently, in the general dental community, it is fast becoming a lost art form. Considering it is the gateway to dental implant therapy and a key to grasping concepts and principles in aesthetic dentistry, the purpose of this presentation is to improve understanding of complete denture therapy based on proven clinical and documented protocols.

title: Composite is My Friend - Adventures in Anterior Guidance
description: Creating a smooth, functional, and beautiful anterior guidance in our esthetic cases requires an understanding of function, anatomy and materials. We will explore how using composite to experiment with anterior relationships can save you time and frustration before you go to porcelain.

title: Whiter, Brighter, Better
description: In this CE webinar, the entire dental team will learn all aspects of tooth whitening. This will include photos, case presentations, tooth bleaching, taking impressions, pouring models, to the fabrication and delivery of the home whitening trays.

title: Implant Retained Overdentures: From Diagnosis to Final, Esthetic Prosthesis
